newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OECD diplomat heads to trade post - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OECD diplomat heads to trade post - report.

text.p: David Aaron, a diplomat in Paris, is President Bill Clinton's choice to become undersecretary of commerce for international trade, the Washington Post reported on Friday, quoting administration sources.
Aaron, 58, was a deputy national security adviser under former President Jimmy Carter, and has served as ambassador to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development since 1993.
If confirmed by the Senate, Aaron would replace Stuart Eizenstat, who has been picked to become undersecretary of state for economic affairs.

The Post also reported in its "In the Loop" column that Clinton has chosen former congressional representative Lindy Boggs, a Democrat from Louisiana and 18-year veteran of the House of Representatives, to be the first woman to be U.S. ambassador to the Vatican.
No comment was immediately available from the White House on the appointments.
